summary: Iter 42 — Verified Internal Document Vault (immutable PDF archive) end-to-end (backend + frontend). Backend pytest suite test_iter42_doc_vault.py: 15/15 PASS covering: GET /api/doc-vault list with default+doc_type=BOL+doc_id+limit filters returning items/count/retention_years=7; GET /api/doc-vault/stats returning total_documents=12, by_type=[{BOL:9, QUOTE:2, RATE_CONFIRMATION:1} with count+bytes+latest], oldest_at, retention_years=7; auto-archive hook on GET /api/documents/{id}/pdf produces +2 rows per double-render with monotonically increasing version numbers and distinct sha256 fingerprints per render; auto-archive hook on GET /api/orisei/rate-confirmations/{rc_id}/pdf writes doc_type=RATE_CONFIRMATION with ref_id=booking_id; auto-archive hook on GET /api/orisei/quotes/{quote_id}/pdf writes doc_type=QUOTE; GET /api/doc-vault/{archive_id} returns metadata incl. payload_snapshot dict; GET /api/doc-vault/{archive_id}/file streams application/pdf with %PDF magic bytes (427,996 bytes for one BOL), Content-Disposition inline, X-Archive-Sha256 + X-Archive-Version response headers; POST /api/doc-vault/{archive_id}/re-render returns {ok:true, next_url} mapping each doc_type to its correct source generator (/api/documents/{id}/pdf for BOL, /api/orisei/rate-confirmations/{id}/pdf for RC, /api/orisei/quotes/{id}/pdf for QUOTE); 404 on unknown archive_id for metadata/file/re-render. Frontend /document-archive: page loads with FMCSA/DOT Document Retention compliance banner, four stat cards (stat-total=12, stat-bytes=4.90 MB, stat-oldest=6/18/2026, stat-retention=7 years), 3 by-type chips (Bill of Lading·9, Freight Quote·2, Rate Confirmation·1), filter-type/filter-doc-id/search-input/refresh-btn all wired, archive-table-body renders 12 row-DA-* entries with View/PDF/Re-issue actions, preview-DA-* click opens archive-preview-modal containing blob: iframe (PDF inline preview). Deep-links verified: /document-archive?doc_id=DOC-DA17EC42 prefills filter-doc-id and shows 8 versioned rows; /document-archive?ref_id=BK-8A6CB0889E shows the 1 matching RC row. Sidebar nav-document-archive (Document Archive (Legal Hold)) navigates to /document-archive. Broker Settings → tab-doc-edit → input[data-testid=doc-id] filled with INV-TEST → doc-history-link appears with text '↳ View immutable version history for INV-TEST' and href=/document-archive?doc_id=INV-TEST; click navigates correctly and prefills the filter. /workflow page after selecting first booking shows workflow-doc-archive-link with href=/document-archive?ref_id=BK-55AE8E2562; click navigates correctly. All acceptance criteria pass.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/doc_vault.py archive_pdf() computes version via count_documents({doc_type, doc_id}) + 1 — this is a race condition under concurrent renders of the same doc_id (two parallel renders both see count=N and both write version=N+1). For an immutable legal archive this is unlikely to matter (operators rarely double-click within ms), but consider a Mongo findAndModify counter or a unique index on (doc_type, doc_id, version) to surface collisions instead of silently producing duplicate version numbers.

routes/doc_vault.py /re-render endpoint returns next_url but does NOT internally re-execute the source endpoint. The docstring acknowledges this (UI is expected to hit next_url itself). This is intentional and well-documented, but means the frontend MUST chain the POST with a follow-up GET to the source URL or the user will see a stale archive_id with no new version. Frontend code in DocumentArchive.jsx does perform this chain — verified via the in-app Re-issue button which produces a fresh v+1 row.

routes/orisei_operations.py rate_con_pdf at line 480 looks up booking via {'booking_id': rc['booking_id']} but brokerage_bookings rows are keyed by 'booked_id' in routes/brokerage.py line 759 (only the legacy 'id' field also exists). Most production brokerage bookings will NOT have a 'booking_id' field, so the booking lookup falls back to {} and the rendered PDF will be missing all booking context (origin/destination/equipment/etc). This is a pre-existing bug in the Rate Con flow, not a regression — but it became visible during iter 42 testing when we had to manually stamp booking_id=booked_id on a booking before the RC PDF would render with real data. RECOMMEND: change line 480-481 to `await db.brokerage_bookings.find_one({'$or':[{'booking_id': rc['booking_id']},{'booked_id': rc['booking_id']}]}, {'_id':0})`.

routes/doc_vault.py archive_pdf payload_snapshot stores entire `rc` and `booking` dicts (potentially with sensitive fields like carrier_contact_email/phone). For a 7-year retention vault this is desirable for re-render fidelity, but ensure the existing PII / GDPR audit pass covers document_archive collection.

DocumentArchive.jsx — Re-issue button POSTs /re-render then chains the source GET; verify the source GET inherits the auth Bearer token from api wrapper (it does — used via api.get) so the new archive row is attributed to the current user, not 'system'. Confirmed during testing: new BOL v9 was attributed to Test Admin.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 42 Document Vault is fully verified. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iter42_doc_vault.py for regression. The suite auto-creates an RC (RC-TESTITER42) if none exist — but expects brokerage_bookings to have a `booking_id` field, which is normally absent (production rows use `booked_id`). If the RC fixture fails with 'Booking not found' on a fresh DB, manually stamp `booking_id: <booked_id>` on a booking via mongo first, OR fix the upstream orisei_operations.py find_one query (see code-review comment #3). Backend stats endpoint counts will grow each test run because every BOL render creates a new version — that is by design (immutable archive) and not a leak.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in the new Document Vault feature itself. The one pre-existing issue surfaced (RC PDF booking lookup using wrong field name) is documented in code-review comments and does not affect the vault auto-archive hook, which fires correctly regardless of whether the booking lookup returns data.
